statements.text: I confirm what Safety-Control Integrator takes from Braking ideas for wind turbines (E42) that spring-applied pads press a disc, which from my side means the caliper reaction must go through the bedplate rails in the nacelle bedplate sketch with brake rails (E58) to the post clamp; the survival thrust (E22) of 37.3 N is a heavy shopping bag, the bending stress (E27) of 16.6 Megapascal (MPa), meaning million newtons per square metre, is about 16 times below the 276 MPa typical yield in the Aluminum 6061-T6 — Material Datasheet (E55) and the 5/12/23, 3:58 PM ASM Material Data Sheet Aluminum 6061-T6; 6061-T651 (E56), with tip bend (E26) 0.516 mm against 25.0 mm side gap.

The side gap 2.50 cm (E74) clears deflection 0.516 mm (E26) with axial stack 36.0 cm (E52) inside 45 cm, thrust 37.3 N (E22) and moment 13.1 N·m (E23) give stress 16.6 MPa (E27) against yield in the Aluminum 6061-T6 — Material Datasheet (E55), power 3.27 W (E11) to shaft 34.7 W (E12) to net 26.0 W (E38) to regulated 22.1 W (E66) at speeds 1.43e+03 RPM (E14) to 3.15e+03 RPM (E13) and volts 6.50 V (E37) to 14.3 V (E36), and stop 0.673 s (E70) to 0 RPM at 10 s against 10 s rule in the CWC 2019 Rules and Requirements Manual_20190104 (E41) with hold 0.800 N·m beating storm 0.480 N·m (E48) and factored 0.720 N·m (E54), while heat 51.1 W (E39) for 84.3 J (E67) against spin 109 J (E47) plus rise 4.35 K (E53) is bulb-level for seconds.

I read the Buck/Boost Converter - 8-40V to 12V/3A | Little Bird Electronics (E60) which accepts 8-40 V input and delivers regulated 12 V, which from structures side means the revised 8.41 V low and 18.5 V top (E76) only move volts inside the body with no added thrust; survival thrust (E22) 37.3 N with moment (E23) 13.1 N·m still give deflection (E26) 0.516 mm and stress (E27) 16.6 Megapascal (MPa), meaning million newtons per square metre, about 17 times below typical 276 MPa yield in the Aluminum 6061-T6 — Material Datasheet (E55), like a heavy shopping bag on a scaffold pole.

Side gap 2.50 cm in the side clearance (E74) clears deflection 0.516 mm in the post tip deflection (E26) with axial stack 36.0 cm in the axial stack length (E52) inside 45 cm, thrust 37.3 N in the survival thrust (E22) with moment 13.1 N-m in the overturning moment (E23) gives stress 16.6 MPa in the bending stress (E27) against yield in the Aluminum 6061-T6 — Material Datasheet (E55), power 3.27 W in the shaft power at 5 m/s (E11) to 22.1 W regulated in the regulated load power (E66) at speeds 1430 RPM in the rpm at 5 m/s (E14) to 3150 RPM in the rpm at 11 m/s (E13), where Revolutions Per Minute (RPM) means shaft turns per minute, and stop 0.673 s in the upgraded stop (E70) to 0 RPM at 10 s against the 10 s rule in the CWC 2019 Rules and Requirements Manual (E41) with hold 0.80 N-m beating storm 0.48 N-m in the electrical-only runaway check (E48) and factored 0.72 N-m in the required hold torque (E54).

For Structures-Survival Engineer, I take up the Aluminum 6061-T6 — Material Datasheet (E55) which gives about 276 MPa yield, which from shutdown side means the spring-brake reaction can be fed into the post without damage during a storm stop.

The survival thrust (E22) 37.3 N with overturning moment (E23) 13.1 N·m still give post deflection (E26) 0.516 mm and bending stress (E27) 16.6 MPa, meaning million newtons per square metre, about one-seventeenth of yield in the Aluminum 6061-T6 Material Datasheet (E55), like a heavy shopping bag on a scaffold pole, while side gap (E74) 2.50 cm clears that bend by about 48 times and axial stack (E52) 36.0 cm sits inside the 45 cm cube with 9 cm spare.

Side gap 2.50 cm in the side clearance (E74) clears deflection 0.516 mm in the post tip deflection (E26) and stack 36.0 cm in the axial stack length (E52) sits inside 45 cm, while thrust 37.3 N in the survival thrust (E22) with moment 13.1 N·m in the overturning moment (E23) gives stress 16.6 MPa in the bending stress (E27) against yield in the Aluminum 6061-T6 — Material Datasheet (E55), all ordinary body-weight and doorway scales.
